"Ravens X10" has three of four top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "Ravens X10" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
808.headline: How much has sold

809.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Gold Bar Bingo" have been sold. The game is near the midpoint of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

The table below shows the full count for "Gold Bar Bingo", with every prize level included.
809.headline: Where this game is in its run

810.body:
One of In the Green's top prizes was claimed over a week ago. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with seven top prizes and now has four top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Today's free summary of "In the Green" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
810.headline: Another top prize was claimed

811.body:
"Extreme Green" has gone close to two months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $1 million prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The second-biggest prize left on "Extreme Green" is $50,000, with two of them remaining.

If "Extreme Green" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
811.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

812.body:
The most common win left on "Loose Change®" is $1. The second biggest prize left is $500, and 35 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "Loose Change®" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 10.
812.headline: The prize table, line by line

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" has 371,165 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with eight left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
813.headline: A close look at the prizes

814.body:
About a third of the tickets for "High Voltage" have been sold. The game is in the middle of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Every line of High Voltage's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
814.headline: How much has sold

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $100,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold seven of the original nine. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

If "$100,000 Crossword" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
815.headline: Someone claimed a $100,000 prize

816.body:
"Deluxe Crossword" has 396,284 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with eleven left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "Deluxe Crossword" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
816.headline: A close look at the prizes

817.body:
"Hello Money!" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed over a week ago. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Everything above about "Hello Money!" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
817.headline: The top prize list got shorter

818.body:
"10X Cash" has 323,490 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1,000 prize, with 32 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "10X Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
818.headline: What's actually left to win

819.body:
"30X Cash" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The table below shows the full count for "30X Cash", with every prize level included.
819.headline: Same price, different prizes

820.body:
"Cozy Cash" is near the start of its run, with most of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "Cozy Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
820.headline: Tickets sold so far

821.body:
"Season's Greetings" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $10,000 was claimed over a week ago. Unsold tickets still hold five of the original six. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Tomorrow's count on "Season's Greetings" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
821.headline: Fewer $10,000 prizes left

822.body:
Only a small slice of the tickets for "Peppermint Payout" are sold. The top prize count has held, with six of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "Peppermint Payout" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
822.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

823.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Holly-Day Cash" have been sold. The game is near the start of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
823.headline: Tickets sold so far

Tomorrow's count on "Winter Multiplier" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
